answer.justification: The target space is the lesser sac (omental bursa), which lies posterior to the stomach and behind the lesser omentum. Its anterior boundary is the gastrohepatic ligament, the free edge of the lesser omentum. Dividing this ligament between the lesser curvature and liver opens the lesser sac, allowing access to the posterior gastric/pancreatic region. The other ligaments do not form this boundary.

decision.reason: This is a basic surgical anatomy fact; the lesser sac posterior to the stomach is accessed by dividing the gastrohepatic ligament, so PubMed is unnecessary.
